original_question: Fix a sufficiently regular window function for the short-time Fourier transform. Which spiral-like or more general sampling sets in the time-frequency plane are informative enough to determine a function, up to global phase, from sampled STFT magnitude measurements?
target_in_paper: Section 8.3, Question 8.7 (the open problem on spiral-like sampling sets for sampled STFT phase retrieval).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the core object of the paper’s question: a fixed sufficiently nice/regular STFT window, magnitude-only sampled STFT data, spiral-like versus more general sampling sets in the time-frequency plane, and uniqueness only up to a global phase.
missing_details: The ambient setting is the continuous one-dimensional STFT problem, not an abstract or discrete time-frequency sampling problem: f is a complex-valued function on R and the sampling set is Ω ⊂ R^2.
The paper’s operator is the STFT V_w f(x, ξ) = ∫_R f(t) w(t - x)e^(-itξ) dt = F[f · S_x w](ξ); your draft leaves this implicit.
The measurements are the sampled magnitudes |V_w f|^2_Ω := {|V_w f(x, ξ)|^2 : (x, ξ) ∈ Ω}.
'Up to global phase' is explicitly the equivalence relation f ~ g iff there exists α ∈ R such that f = e^(iα) g.
The nearby context is Section 8.3 on compactly supported functions; your draft omits this paper-faithful scope and so reads slightly broader than Question 8.7.

Because the paragraph immediately after Question 8.7 treats recovery of arbitrary f ∈ L2(R) as a separate question (Question 8.8), a stand-alone rewrite should not silently broaden Question 8.7 to all of L2(R).
The paper states only that the window is sufficiently 'nice'; replacing that by a materially stronger hypothesis would go beyond the paper.
The question is about uniqueness/injectivity, not stability bounds, algorithm design, blind recovery, or discrete WDD formulas.
refined_question: Fix B > 0 and a sufficiently "nice" window function w in L2(R). In the one-dimensional sampled short-time Fourier transform phase retrieval problem for compactly supported complex-valued signals f in L2(R) with support(f) ⊂ [-B,B], where V_w f(x, ξ) = ∫_R f(t) w(t - x)e^(-itξ) dt, for which spiral-like—and, more generally, for which sampling sets Ω ⊂ R^2—do the sampled magnitude measurements {|V_w f(x, ξ)|^2 : (x, ξ) ∈ Ω} determine f uniquely up to a global phase, i.e. modulo the relation f ~ g iff there exists α ∈ R with f = e^(iα)g?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Question 8.7 because the phrase 'spiral-like sampling sets' appears there verbatim. The surrounding text defines the exact STFT model, the sampled measurement notation, and the global-phase equivalence relation. It also shows that Question 8.7 sits inside the compactly supported/bandlimited discussion of Section 8.3, while the broader problem of recovering arbitrary L2(R) signals is explicitly separated out as Question 8.8. So the faithful refinement is to make the one-dimensional continuous STFT setup and injectivity-modulo-phase formulation explicit, without broadening the problem to all L2(R), to stability, or to algorithms.
